sentences.text: Streptospondylus was a medium-sized megalosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of France, measuring about 6 meters long and weighing roughly 500 kilograms.
Scientists identify this animal by the unique bifurcation of the hypapophyses in its anterior dorsal vertebrae.
The vertebrae of this predator were scientifically described in 1808 as the very first dinosaur remains ever found.
Georges Cuvier initially misidentified these early bones as crocodilian elements when he first examined them.
Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer later renamed the species Streptospondylus altdorfensis in 1832 because the vertebrae were opisthocoel, meaning convex in front and concave behind.
This genus was earlier assigned to crocodilian groups in the 19th century but is typically classified in the Megalosauridae in the 20th century.
A 2010 cladistic analysis suggested that Streptospondylus was the sister species of Magnosaurus within the Megalosauridae.
However, Carrano et al. placed Streptospondylus at Megalosauria incertae sedis in 2012 due to its fragmentary nature.
Streptospondylus lived during the Callovian to Oxfordian stages, from 165.3 to 159 million years ago.
